Now independent verification: diff with LC_ALL=C sort -u data/b.txt. Note: sort -u on words separated by spaces/newlines — sort treats lines, so "pear apple pear plum Apple apple" is one line. It would not produce the same. So I need to apply tr as well. The acceptance check says verify with `sort -u data/b.txt`. Under sort -u, lines are compared; line1 = "pear apple pear plum Apple apple", line2="fig plum". They're distinct lines, so output would be those two lines — not matching. Hmm.

The task says "independently verify with `sort -u data/b.txt` (note: shell sort -u under the C locale is case-sensitive byte order) or `LC_ALL=C sort -u data/b.txt`, confirming it matches your output."

That's problematic since data/b.txt has multiple words per line. To match, need tokenization first. The intended independent verification presumably: `tr -s '[:space:]' '\n' < data/b.txt | LC_ALL=C sort -u`. Let me run both and report the real output honestly. Run `LC_ALL=C sort -u data/b.txt` and show it doesn't directly match (because it sorts lines, not tokens), then run the tokenized version to confirm.

Also could build a Python independent implementation that splits whitespace, dedups, sorts by Unicode code point (case-sensitive), and diff.

Let me run these commands.
